There is a lot of discussion today about AI recruitment. Is it all bots?

Here is how OJ is currently recruiting:

After putting out a public notice to gather proposals for an analyst, we evaluated them but then also three of us personally drove to a local Ivy League business MBA program, sat down for meetings, and talked with graduates over coffee.

That was super high signal.

After that, we followed up, and they excited our other partners in a zoom interview, or didn’t. The right people can assert themselves across multiple mediums. We’re highly engaged for super-interested talent only.

My takeaways:
-Elite employers are of course recruiting face to face. People will travel for talent, as we did.
-Elite colleges matter. Speaking for ourselves, we go to the best.
-But I was a trailer park kid. I went to state schools. I was never Ivy.
-OJ seeks out extraordinary enthusiasm and talent, but doesn’t care where it comes from if excellence is demonstrated. If someone has an extraordinary story and wants to work for us, let us know.
https://t.co/tLu7vEvP6y 

We seek to find talent in all forms, while warning that the baseline is very high.

🚨$NVDA cuts neocloud support plans down $1B q/q and adds tighter language around conditions; removes revenue share language from last quarter; adds new language that certain commitments "could be reduced or eliminated" if contingencies are not satisfactorily resolved. Cuts previously disclosed 2028 capex $1B to zero (sounds like a project pushout or cancellation).

Now says commitments take effect "only if the neoclouds secure financing to purchase the infrastructure products and the related compute capacity is deployed, made operational, and accepted by us."

Previous language: "We continue to make commitments....Under these agreements we will earn revenue on upfront sale of our infra and if certain criteria are met, we will participate in revenue share."

Re: secondary equity investments, future commitments fall from $25B to $20B but 2028 plans rise from $3B --> $11B. Unclear if this is pushouts from 2027 investments not made (such as Figure AI).

Bottom line: Total commitments grew 41% QoQ, driven almost entirely by a surge in 2028 supply/capacity commitments and long-dated data center leases, but the new contingency clause means a large portion is conditional on neoclouds securing external financing.

Also 10-Q to arrive "in coming weeks" seems like a delay.
